summary: Full read of 20 SEC whistleblower award orders (Oct 2022 - May 2023). Adds 23 case rows: 3 award rows (Claimant 4 in Release 96231 with nearly $1,600,000; Claimants 2 and 3 in Release 96399, no amounts) and 20 denial rows (contested denials with reasons, and uncontested denials of other claimants mentioned in footnotes); 1 event (Jan 2023 order cutting an award because the claimant offered to trade the tip for a settlement); 43 suggested corrections adding how each claimant qualified, reductions, insider status and fixes (96641 amount is "approximately", not "over"; 96705 does print a total; 97051 has two joint claimants). Percentages, sanctions and targets are redacted in nearly all orders.

cases.quote: Claimant 4) receive a whistleblower award of nearly $1,600,000
cases.summary: Award to a separate claimant whose independent analysis of public filings significantly contributed to an accounting-fraud action; request for a higher share and claim to have been the source of the joint claimants' tip rejected.
cases.notes: Exchange Act Release No. 96231, File No. 2023-13. Amount as printed: "nearly": upper bound; percentage redacted (equal to the joint award of Claimants 1-3, whose contributions the Commission found equal in significance). Claimant 4 contested the Preliminary Determinations; the CRS recommendation was adopted unchanged. Original information through independent analysis of public filings (outsider, specialised accounting knowledge). Earlier submissions did not meet the Rule 21F-9 TCR requirements, later Form TCR submissions did. Claimed hardships (threats of litigation, harassment) not substantiated enough for an increase. Anonymous.

cases.quote: It is further ORDERED that Claimant 2's whistleblower award application in the Covered Action be, and hereby is, denied.
cases.summary: Award claim denied: the information was given by an entity the claimant owns, not by the claimant as an individual, and the claimant filed a Form TCR eighteen months late; Section 36(a) waiver refused.
cases.notes: Exchange Act Release No. 96439, File No. 2023-19. Claimant 2 (owner and founder of the entity) contested, arguing the entity's general counsel acted at his/her direction and blaming ineffective counsel; rejected. Applies Rule 21F-2(a)(2) (an entity cannot be a whistleblower) and the Rule 21F-9(e) 30-day TCR requirement to pending applications. Anonymous. This order was later vacated: Release No. 99890 (April 3, 2024), after a voluntary remand from the Fifth Circuit, found Claimant 2 a whistleblower, waived the late TCR under Section 36(a) and granted him an award of more than $400,000.

events.title: SEC cuts an award because the whistleblower offered to withhold the tip in exchange for a settlement from the company
events.description: In an award order the Commission gave a lower percentage to a claimant who, through counsel, tried to trade the tip for a cash settlement from the company and offered to withhold it from the SEC, finding this contrary to the law enforcement interest and the goals of the programme.
events.quote: the whistleblower program does not condone a claimant attempting to trade a whistleblower tip for a monetary payment from the company allegedly engaged in the misconduct.

gaps: Award percentages, sanctions amounts, respondents and dates are redacted in most orders; nothing more can be taken from the documents.

suggested_corrections.value: Award to a prospective investor who reported an ongoing offering fraud, prompting the investigation; TCR filing requirements waived.

Exchange Act Release No. 96129, File No. 2023-06. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Oct. 24, 2022). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "over $400,000": lower bound; percentage redacted. Outsider (a prospective investor). The Commission used its Section 36(a) exemptive authority to waive the Rule 21F-9(b)/(c) TCR requirements: the claimant filed an anonymous online TCR personally under counsel's name and signed counsel's certification. Assistance: documents, interview, testimony. Part of the reasoning is redacted. Covered action and sanctions redacted; no other claimants mentioned.
Award for information of great significance that led to the return of a significant amount of money to harmed investors; claimant met Enforcement staff twice.

Exchange Act Release No. 96178, File No. 2023-07. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Oct. 31, 2022). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "more than $10 million": lower bound; percentage redacted. Not contested. Qualified under Rule 21F-4(c)(2) (significantly contributed). Insider status not stated. Covered action and sanctions redacted; no other claimants mentioned.

Joint award to three claimants (Claimants 1, 2 and 3) whose analysis of accounting data and non-public information caused staff to inquire into new conduct in an existing investigation; to be split 33.33% each unless they ask otherwise.

Exchange Act Release No. 96231, File No. 2023-13. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Nov. 4, 2022). This row is the joint award to Claimants 1, 2 and 3 (one "whistleblower" under Section 21F(a)(6), joint tip); the separate award of nearly $1,600,000 to Claimant 4 is its own row. Amount as printed: "nearly": upper bound; percentage redacted. Not contested. Original information from independent knowledge and independent analysis; not excluded by Rule 21F-8(c)(4) (audit) although Claimant 3's role is redacted. OWB to pay each 33.33% unless they jointly request another split within ten days. Settled action against a company; sanctions redacted, paid in full.

Award reduced for culpability and unreasonable reporting delay: the claimant took part briefly, at a supervisor's direction, in part of the conduct and waited over two years to report; three other claims denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 96381, File No. 2023-17. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (Nov. 28, 2022). Whistleblowers awarded: 1 (Claimant 1). Award amount as printed; percentage redacted. Not contested. Insider involved in the conduct; percentage set to account for culpability and a reporting delay of over two years; information covered only part of the action. Settled administrative action against a company, sanctions redacted and fully paid. Claimants 2 and 5 and a set of joint claimants denied (separate rows).
Award to Claimant 1, whose information contributed to the decision to open the investigation and guided its early stages; the claimant had raised concerns internally at the companies.

Exchange Act Release No. 96399, File No. 2023-18. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (Nov. 29, 2022). Three awards in one order: this row is Claimant 1's award; Claimants 2 and 3 are separate rows. No dollar amount; percentages redacted. Not contested. Claimant 1 reported internally first (positive factor). Covered action: litigated court action against two individuals and two companies; sanctions redacted. Denials: Claimant 4 (contested), one other claimant (uncontested), and Claimants 2 and 3 on a separate action (separate rows).
pp. 3-4 and p. 6, Claimant 1 (Release No. 96399)
Award for information that revealed a fraud and prompted the opening of the investigation; the charges were based on it. Another claim denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 96439, File No. 2023-19. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (Dec. 2, 2022). Whistleblowers awarded: 1 (Claimant 1). Amount as printed: "nearly": upper bound; percentage redacted. Not contested. Qualified by causing the investigation to open (several interviews, documents, help identifying witnesses and drafting subpoenas). Insider status not stated. Settled civil action in federal district court; sanctions redacted, collected. Claimant 2 denied (separate row). Vacated by Release No. 99890 (April 3, 2024), which re-determined the claims: Claimant 1 more than $2,000,000 and Claimant 2 more than $400,000 (rows from that order).

Award reduced for a four-year unreasonable reporting delay: the claimant reported only after receiving an SEC subpoena about his/her own conduct in an unrelated matter; recommended offset against that matter's unpaid sanctions dropped.

Exchange Act Release No. 96604, File No. 2023-22. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Jan. 6, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "nearly": upper bound; percentage redacted. Claimant contested the percentage and the offset; percentage kept, but the Commission decided not to offset the award against amounts the claimant owed in an unrelated SEC matter. Tip caused the investigation to open; information from the claimant's work and independent analysis (occupation redacted). Submission still voluntary because the earlier subpoena concerned unrelated subject matter. Settled administrative proceeding against a company (cease-and-desist, censure, disgorgement, interest, penalty; amounts redacted, paid in full).

Award on four covered actions (with individual actions from the same facts) and four related actions by another agency; information let the SEC act sooner, potentially preventing further misappropriation.

Exchange Act Release No. 96641, File No. 2023-23. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Jan. 12, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "approximately $900,000" (total recommended for the Covered Actions and the Other Agency Actions, based on current collections), not a lower bound; percentages redacted. Not contested. Claimant's request to count all funds collected by the receiver as collections refused; only amounts distributed to investors by the court-appointed receiver are treated as collected sanctions. Insider status not stated. One other claimant denied (separate row).

Awards to two claimants; Claimant 1's share kept low because he/she, through counsel, offered to withhold the tip from the SEC in exchange for a cash settlement from the company. Two other claims denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 96642, File No. 2023-24. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Jan. 12, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 2. Amount as printed: "approximately $300,000": the anticipated combined payment to both claimants based on current collections; percentages redacted (the CRS revised them on reconsideration). Claimant 1 (employee of the company, an insider; raised concerns internally) caused the investigation to open; contested the percentage; no finding of unreasonable delay. Claimant 2 (uncontested) caused staff to expand the investigation to different conduct. Settled cease-and-desist proceeding with a civil penalty (amount redacted). Two other claimants denied (separate row).
Award to a claimant whose information opened the investigation and helped shape strategy, identify witnesses and draft subpoenas; the claimant had reported internally first. Another claim denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 96656, File No. 2023-25. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Order (PDF)" (Jan. 13, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 1 (Claimant 1). Amount as printed: "more than": lower bound; percentage redacted. Not contested. Initial submissions without a Form TCR opened the investigation; a later Form TCR through counsel with new information that significantly contributed gave an independent basis for eligibility. Reported internally first (positive factor). Administrative proceeding; sanctions redacted, fully collected. Claimant 2 denied (separate row).

Awards to three claimants in a fraud case paid from receiver distributions to investors; the first, an insider, was the main basis for opening the investigation, the other two added less. Two claims denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 96705, File No. 2023-30. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (Jan. 19, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 3. Amount printed as "will total around $18 [redaction] million": the expected total for all three awarded claimants, based on anticipated distributions to harmed investors by the court-appointed receiver (counted as collected sanctions); per-claimant percentages redacted. Claimant 1 (an insider, uncontested) gave the main basis for opening the investigation; Claimants 2 and 3 contested for higher shares, refused (information partly duplicative and later). No reduction for reporting delay. Two claimants denied (separate rows).
Award to a claimant whose tip opened the investigation of a broker-dealer and who helped identify witnesses and shape the investigative plan. Three other claims denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 96765, File No. 2023-33. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (Jan. 30, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 1 (Claimant 1). Amount as printed: "about"; percentage redacted. Not contested. Settled action against a registered broker-dealer (disgorgement, prejudgment interest and civil penalty, amounts redacted, all collected). Insider status not stated. Claimant 2 (late claim) and two other claimants denied (separate rows).

Award on an SEC action and a related criminal action for highly significant information on a fraudulent offering scheme that helped identify previously unknown participants; conditioned on waiving an award from another agency's programme.

Exchange Act Release No. 96887, File No. 2023-35. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Feb. 13, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "almost": upper bound; covers both the covered action and a related criminal action (percentages redacted). Not contested. Information given during an existing investigation (significant contribution). The related action was found more directly connected to the SEC programme than to another agency's whistleblower programme (redacted), where the claimant also applied; the related-action award is conditioned on an irrevocable waiver of that claim (Rule 21F-3(b)(3)). Claims on two other actions and two other claimants denied (separate rows).
Maximum 30% award under the Rule 21F-6(c) presumption: the claimant acted quickly, advanced the investigation and kept helping; nothing collected yet.

Exchange Act Release No. 96923, File No. 2023-36. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Feb. 14, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. The order gives no dollar amount; percentage stated: 30%, by the Rule 21F-6(c) presumption (maximum award not expected to exceed $5 million, no negative factors). Not contested. Court judgment against the defendants offset by restitution and forfeiture in a parallel criminal action; the claimant benefits from criminal-action collections; "To date, there have been no collections in the Covered Action or the parallel criminal action." One other claimant denied (separate row).
Joint award to two claimants who promptly reported a fraud to another agency, which shared it with the SEC and prompted the investigation; to be split 50% each unless they ask otherwise.

Exchange Act Release No. 97051, File No. 2023-41. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (March 7, 2023). Joint award to two whistleblowers acting jointly (footnote 1: "between the two of them"), treated as one whistleblower under Section 21F(a)(6) because they filed together via the same counsel; OWB to pay each 50% unless they jointly request otherwise within ten days. Amount as printed: "approximately"; percentage redacted. Information first given to another agency, then a TCR filed. Insider status not stated; part of the reasoning redacted. No other claimants mentioned.

Award to an outsider who used specialised access and expertise to analyse facts in a case against a company and its executives (independent analysis); the conduct would have been hard to detect otherwise.

Exchange Act Release No. 97295, File No. 2023-050. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (April 13, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "almost": upper bound; percentage redacted. Original information through independent analysis (Rule 21F-4(b)(3)) of a case against the company (type of case redacted). Tip alerted Enforcement staff. Covered action and sanctions redacted; no other claimants mentioned.
Award to a claimant whose tip opened the investigation of a broker-dealer and who helped identify witnesses and shape the investigative plan. Two other claims denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 97285, File No. 2023-49. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (April 11, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 1 (Claimant 1). Amount as printed: "about"; percentage redacted. Not contested. Settled action against a registered broker-dealer (disgorgement, interest, civil penalty; amounts redacted, all collected). Reasoning nearly identical to Release No. 96765. Insider status not stated. Claimant 2 (late claim) and one other claimant denied (separate rows).
Maximum 30% award (more than $3,000) under the Rule 21F-6(c) presumption for a tip that opened the investigation of a fraudulent scheme; multiple interviews.

Exchange Act Release No. 97524, File No. 2023-58. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (May 18, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "more than $3,000": lower bound; percentage stated: 30%, by the Rule 21F-6(c) presumption (maximum award would not exceed $5 million, no negative factors). Tip caused the staff to open the investigation (Rule 21F-4(c)(1)); charges based in part on it. Covered action and sanctions redacted; no other claimants mentioned.
Award for substantial ongoing assistance (multiple contacts, documents, testimony) that helped expedite the investigation.

Exchange Act Release No. 97573, File No. 2023-60. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (May 25, 2023). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "more than": lower bound; percentage redacted. Not contested. Part of the reasoning redacted. Insider status not stated. Covered action and sanctions redacted; no other claimants mentioned.
Larger award to the claimant whose tips, sent persistently for years before the investigation opened, were its initial source; claimant suffered hardships.

Exchange Act Release No. 97598, File No. 2023-61. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (May 26, 2023). This row is Claimant 1. Amount as printed: "about"; percentage redacted. Not contested. The order says Claimant 1 had publicly disclosed his/her identity as a whistleblower, but the order does not name him/her (name redacted). Settled administrative and cease-and-desist proceeding against a firm (disgorgement, interest, penalty; amounts redacted, fully collected). Claimant 2 is a separate row; four other claimants denied (separate row).

Smaller award to a percipient witness whose share was reduced for unreasonable reporting delay (at least five years after knowing, four after leaving the employer); claim that the first claimant's information came from him/her rejected.

Exchange Act Release No. 97598, File No. 2023-61. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (May 26, 2023). This row is Claimant 2. Amount as printed: "about"; percentage redacted. Contested; CRS recommendation adopted. Former employee of the firm (insider); reduced for unreasonable reporting delay, tempered because he/she gave Claimant 1 information knowing it was forwarded to the SEC. Arguments about redactions rejected: Section 21F(h)(2) requires redacting a whistleblower's identity even if he/she went public.
